title: 13-year-old stabbed in broad daylight attack in the Bronx
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A teenage boy was stabbed in broad daylight outside a Bronx supermarket Saturday and left wounded, police sources said.

The 13-year-old was stabbed in the stomach outside C-Town at 1612 Westchester Avenue in the Bronx’s Soundview neighborhood at 5:23pm, police sources said.

He was taken to Jacoby Hospital on Pelham Parkway by EMS workers after the assault and is in stable condition.

Blood could be seen on the concrete sidewalk at the scene as a group of police officers cordoned off the area in front of the store.

No arrests have been made in the incident and the search for the assailant is ongoing, according to police sources.

The heinous attack comes days after a New York City Schools employee was stabbed to death by an lunatic who had 13 prior arrests.

NYC Department of Education Paraprofessional Rashaun Shettlewood, 32, was fatally stabbed in the chest and his 33-year-old friend was stabbed in the torso by the brute in another daytime attack in the Bronx at Davidson and West Tremont Avenues in Morris Heights at 3:30 pm.

The men were transported to St. Barnabas Hospital where Shettlewood succumbed to his injuries, his friend was in stable condition, police sources said.

It was unclear what led to the attack, but police source said it stemmed from a dispute.

The alleged stabber, Jeffrey Jorge, 37, of Brooklyn, was arrested the following morning after cops spotted him wielding a knife at Ocean Avenue and Parkside Avenue in Prospect-Lefferts Gardens.

He was charged with murder, attempted murder, manslaughter and two counts each of assault and criminal possession of a weapon, according to the NYPD.
